clue.text: 21 men once carried this young woman on dock

parts.note: to dock is to cut short
a lass is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Sailors of old seem to be lugging a girl along the quayside.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is the cross-reference to 21 across, AT SEA, so '21 men' are seafarers. The wordplay reads back to front: the young woman sits on top of the dock.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is the short curved sword that pirates and naval sailors once wore as a sidearm.

clue.text: Replaces spittoon containing pool of foul liquid

indicators.note: the words together hold the solution inside them, running across the gap

parts.note: the letters sit inside these two words, across the word break

explanation.surface: Someone swaps a spittoon for one holding a puddle of nasty fluid.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit is a pit for sewage and waste water, a pool of foul liquid.

clue.text: Random dirty hack affected everybody

indicators.note: the letters are affected, meaning altered or disturbed from their original order

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: A sleazy journalist picked at random has harmed the whole population.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Random' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the letters; 'affected' does the shuffling.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names three common first names to mean ordinary people in general, anyone at all.

clue.text: George Best estate has raised a fortune

indicators.note: the first word has, or holds, the second inside it
in a down entry the letter a is lifted from the bottom to the top, rotating the whole word

parts.note: Utopia is the ideal state, the best estate imaginable
one's lot is one's fortune or destiny

explanation.surface: The estate of the footballer George Best has made a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: George is a traditional nickname for an aircraft's automatic pilot. 'George Best' tempts as one name, but it splits into definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilots in RAF slang called the automatic flight control system George, so the name stands for it.

clue.text: Doctor sounds surprised about smashing result

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the exclamations people make when surprised, as in oohs and ahs

explanation.surface: A physician gasps in amazement at a terrific outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashing' looks like praise for a great result, but it means breaking something.
explanation.definitionFit: A shard is a sharp broken piece of glass or pottery, what is left after something shatters.

clue.text: Scratch round opening of Porsche's exhaust

indicators.note: one word going round another wraps it, holding the other inside

parts.note: to scratch something out is to delete it

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its very first letter

parts.note: first letter of Porsche

explanation.surface: A car owner rubs a scratch around the opening of the Porsche's exhaust pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like a car's tailpipe noun, but it is the verb meaning to use up.
explanation.definitionFit: To deplete a supply is to use it up, the same as exhausting it.

clue.text: Treat a lord with contempt in speech and make a quick exit

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so a phrase is chosen for its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: to dis someone is slang for disrespecting them, and a lord is a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: Someone insults a nobleman to his face and then bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase is spoken as a three-word sentence, which then runs together into one verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear is to vanish from sight, which is what someone making a swift getaway does.

clue.text: Precious material in ring worn by queen

indicators.note: something worn by another is put on around it, so the first word surrounds the second

parts.note: a ring of bells is a peal
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A jewel set in a ring the queen is wearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as a piece of jewellery, which suits the pearl, but it is the sound of church bells.
explanation.definitionFit: Pearl is a valuable gem substance formed inside oysters, prized in jewellery.

clue.text: Correct all items damaged in violent upheaval

indicators.note: what is damaged is broken up, so these letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: Fix everything that was broken in the riot.
explanation.definitionFit: A thunderstorm with lightning is a violent disturbance of the weather.

clue.text: Put in case for appeal related to food processing facility

parts.note: to put data in is to enter it

indicators.note: a case is the outside casing, so only the outer letters of the word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of appeal

explanation.surface: A lawyer files a case for an appeal concerning a food factory.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'food processing facility' is the gut, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteral means involving the intestines, the part of the body that digests food.

clue.text: Unclear second issue published additional books

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
to issue is to emit
a newspaper that ran a story published it
spare as in extra, additional
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Confusion over a second edition of a book that came out with extra volumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something semitransparent lets only some light through, so it is not fully clear.

clue.text: Pages bearing ring for groom

indicators.note: the outer word carries the inner one, holding it within itself

parts.note: PP is the standard abbreviation for pages
a rim is a ring around the edge of something

explanation.surface: Page boys carry the ring at a wedding, for the bridegroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groom' is not the bridegroom but the verb, to tidy one's appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to make small fussy improvements to one's appearance, just as to groom oneself.

clue.text: Old pirate misused instrument going through locks

indicators.note: words that are misused are put wrongly, so the letters get out of order

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: An aged buccaneer abuses some tool while breaking through the locks of a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests door locks or canal locks, but here they are locks of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A depilator is a device that removes hair, so it passes through the locks it strips.

clue.text: Subjective view will exploit perk of job?

parts.note: one's take on something is a personal view of it
to will something to an heir is to leave it to them

explanation.surface: A personal opinion that someone will take advantage of their job's fringe benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads like the future tense, but it is the verb meaning to bequeath. The question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Annual paid holiday is a job benefit, and taking leave uses up that benefit.

clue.text: Sober sailor sent to collect money

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: to collect something is to gather it in, so it ends up inside the other word

parts.note: taken as written
tin is old slang for money

explanation.surface: A teetotal seaman is sent out to pick up the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abstinent refrains from alcohol, so they are sober.

clue.text: China impounds contents of this vessel

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something away inside an enclosure

parts.note: china is Cockney rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so a pal

indicators.note: the contents of a word are what lies inside it, its middle letters without the outer ones

parts.note: the middle two letters of this

explanation.surface: Porcelain that holds whatever is in this pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like porcelain, which suits a vessel, but it is rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle, a container for liquids such as medicine.

clue.text: Pass on support for each reporter's way of making progress

parts.note: a prop is a support
as in a pound a head, a means for each

indicators.note: a reporter speaks the news, so the word is given by how it is said

parts.note: a gait is a way of walking along

explanation.surface: Pass on backing for every journalist's method of getting ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pass on' could mean die or decline; here it is spreading something onward.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to spread or transmit something, such as ideas or plants, which is to pass it on.

clue.text: Male individual that originally created an impression?

definitions.text: Male individual that originally created an impression?

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male
one individual is one

indicators.note: originally points to the beginning, so only a word's first letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of that

explanation.surface: A man who first made an impression on others.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: his painting Impression, Sunrise gave the Impressionist movement its name.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude Monet's canvas Impression, Sunrise inspired the term Impressionism, so he literally created the first Impression.

clue.text: Teacher regularly ignoring attempt to go wrong

parts.note: Miss is how British schoolchildren address a female teacher

indicators.note: ignoring every other letter at regular intervals leaves only alternate ones

parts.note: second, fourth and sixth letters of attempt

explanation.surface: A teacher habitually overlooks a pupil's effort to misbehave.
explanation.definitionFit: To misstep is to take a wrong step, so to slip up or err.

clue.text: Rogue star upset body double

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: A wayward film star gets annoyed by the actor standing in for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A surrogate is a substitute who stands in for another person, like a body double on a film set.

clue.text: Promoted partner after demerger dealt with new organisation

parts.note: once the partnership has split, the partner is a former one

indicators.note: a new organisation means things set out in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: A business partner moved up after the company split was handled by the new firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demerger' sounds like corporate jargon, but it just means a couple split up.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exalted has been raised to a high rank, so they have been promoted.

clue.text: Throw away about 50% of what's used for training and education?

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: to sling something away is to throw it away

indicators.note: fifty per cent means keeping exactly half of the word and dropping the rest

parts.note: a choo-choo is a child's word for a train

explanation.surface: Discarding half of the gear used in training and teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Training' hides travel by train: a choo-choo is nursery talk for a train, and half of it is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Schooling is the instruction a person receives, another word for their education.

clue.text: Some microbes emulsify fat

indicators.note: only some of the letters across these words are taken, a run lying inside them

parts.note: the letters sit inside these two words, across the word break

explanation.surface: A science note: certain bacteria break fat down into an emulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fat' looks like a noun, the substance microbes work on, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese describes someone very overweight, that is, extremely fat.

clue.text: Network infiltrated by New Labour

indicators.note: something infiltrated has an intruder slipped inside it

parts.note: a grid is a network, such as the electricity grid
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A political network secretly entered by New Labour, Tony Blair's rebranded party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Labour' reads as one name, but it splits: 'New' gives a letter and 'Labour' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grind is hard, monotonous work, so it means toil or labour.

clue.text: All over the place, in the main

definitions.meaning: second meaning: on the ocean, the main being an old word for the sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as 'mostly', but the main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both confused and lost, and literally out on the ocean in a ship.

clue.text: What may be read as 221?

parts.note: surface reading: a puzzle about how a number is read aloud
setter's reading: 2 and 21 are entries in this grid, 2 down (all the men) plus 21 across (on the ocean), and the result is a comic novel one may read

explanation.walkthrough: Put the answers to 2 down and 21 across side by side and you get three chaps afloat, the title of Jerome K Jerome's 1889 comic novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The book follows three friends on a boating holiday up the Thames, so it is three men out on the water.

clue.text: This may be required to enter an empty ground

definitions.text: This may be required to enter

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed up, so the letters are broken and remixed

parts.note: the letters are used as written

explanation.surface: Admission to a deserted football ground still costs something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a sports stadium, but it is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry fee is a sum handed over before admission, so it is a payment needed to get in.

clue.text: One consumed by fear had visions

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so it ends up inside the other word

parts.note: dread is great fear
one as in oneself, myself, giving me

explanation.surface: Someone eaten up by fear saw hallucinations.
explanation.definitionFit: To have visions in one's sleep is to have dreamed.
